articles.title: Kentucky woman rejects $26 million offer to turn her farm into a data center
articles.summary: A "major artificial intelligence company" reportedly offered a Kentucky women $26 million to build a data center on their farm.

articles.title: Anthropic hands Claude Code more control, but keeps it on a leash
articles.summary: Anthropic’s new auto mode for Claude Code lets AI execute tasks with fewer approvals, reflecting a broader shift toward more autonomous tools that balance speed with safety through built-in safeguards.

articles.title: Spotify tests new tool to stop AI slop from being attributed to real artists
articles.summary: The idea behind the new tool is to give artists more control over which tracks are associated with their name on Spotify.

articles.title: Databricks bought two startups to underpin its new AI security product
articles.summary: With an overflowing war chest from its recent $5 billion raise, Databricks is buying startups and looking for more. It acquired Antimatter and SiftD.ai.

articles.title: Arm is releasing the first in-house chip in its 35-year history
articles.summary: Arm is producing its own CPU for the first time. It developed the CPU with Meta, which is also the chip's first customer.

articles.title: OpenAI’s plans to make ChatGPT more like Amazon aren’t going so well
articles.summary: OpenAI says it's moving away from Instant Checkout, which allowed users to buy items directly through the ChatGPT interface.

articles.title: Google TV’s new Gemini features keep fans updated on sports teams and more
articles.summary: Three Gemini-powered features are coming to your Google TV. This includes visual responses, deep dives, and sports briefs.

articles.title: OpenAI adds open source tools to help developers build for teen safety
articles.summary: Rather than working from scratch to figure out how to make AI safer for teens, developers can use these policies to fortify what they build.

articles.title: Talat’s AI meeting notes stay on your machine, not in the cloud
articles.summary: The subscription-free AI meeting notes app is a local-first twist on notetaking tools like Granola.

articles.title: Doss raises $55M for AI inventory management that plugs into ERP
articles.summary: Doss's AI-powered inventory management system integrates with existing ERP systems. The Series B round was co-led by Madrona and Premji Invest.

articles.title: Meet the former Apple designer building a new AI interface at Hark
articles.summary: The company said it would design models, hardware, and interfaces in tandem to deliver a "seamless end-to-end personal intelligence product."

articles.title: Mirage raises $75M to continue building models for its AI video-editing app Captions
articles.summary: Mirage, the maker of video-editing app Captions, has raised $75 million in growth financing from General Catalyst's Customer Value Fund (CVF).

articles.title: Agile Robots becomes the latest robotics company to partner with Google DeepMind
articles.summary: Agile Robots will incorporate Google DeepMind's robotics foundation models into its bots while collecting data for the AI research lab.

articles.title: Air Street becomes one of the largest solo VCs in Europe with $232M fund
articles.summary: London’s Air Street Capital has raised a large Fund III with eyes locked on backing early-stage European and North American AI companies.

articles.title: Bernie Sanders’ AI ‘gotcha’ video flops, but the memes are great
articles.summary: Sen. Bernie Sanders thinks he's tricked Claude into revealing the AI industry's secrets, but he really just exposed how agreeable chatbots can become.

articles.title: Vibe-coding startup Lovable is on the hunt for acquisitions
articles.summary: Lovable's founder said the fast-growing vibe-coding startup is looking for startups and teams to join its company.

articles.title: Apple sets June date for WWDC 2026, teasing ‘AI advancements’
articles.summary: Apple will host its next Worldwide Developers Conference the week of June 8. The company is expected to announce major updates to Siri with advanced AI capabilities.

articles.title: Startup Gimlet Labs is solving the AI inference bottleneck in a surprisingly elegant way
articles.summary: Gimlet Labs just raised an $80 million Series A for tech that lets AI run across NVIDIA, AMD, Intel, ARM, Cerebras and d-Matrix chips, simultaneously.

articles.title: Littlebird raises $11M for its AI-assisted ‘recall’ tool that reads your computer screen
articles.summary: Littlebird is building an AI that reads your screen in real time to capture context, answer questions, and automate tasks, without relying on screenshots.

articles.title: Elizabeth Warren calls Pentagon’s decision to bar Anthropic ‘retaliation’
articles.summary: In a letter to Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, Senator Elizabeth Warren (D-MA) equated the DOD's decision to label Anthropic a "supply-chain risk" as retaliation, arguing that the Pentagon could simply have terminated its contract with the AI lab.

articles.title: Digital Realty plans Milan data center development
articles.summary: Company buys land outside Milan, first phase due live in 2028

articles.title: Alabama-based Construction Partners to build data center as part of corporate headquarters
articles.summary: Details about data center are unclear

articles.summary: US gov’t will contribute $250m towards the investment

articles.summary: Raz Elad, founder and CEO of Israeli chip startup NextSilicon, on how his firm can take on Nvidia. Maybe

articles.title: Marshall Islands to connect to Google’s Halaihai subsea cable
articles.summary: Island nation to deploy branch linking to search giant's upcoming cable

articles.title: Aker BP to deploy Armada Edge data center on Norwegian oil rig
articles.summary: Follows recent ageement between Armada and Aker-backed Nscale

articles.title: BT signs £200m connectivity contract with Northern Ireland Electricity Networks
articles.summary: BT will also provide cybersecurity and IT services to NIE Networks

articles.title: Metrobloks announces plans for three-building data center campus in Kansas City, Missouri
articles.summary: Company to invest $1.4 billion in project

articles.title: Cerebras plans data center in Manitoba, Canada
articles.summary: Following Saskatchewan announcement with Bell

articles.title: FCC bans all foreign-produced routers over "unacceptable risks to national security"
articles.summary: Imports of consumer-grade foreign-made routers subject to Covered List over cybersecurity and supply chain vulnerabilities

articles.title: Microsoft agrees to lease 700MW at Crusoe's data center in Abilene, Texas - report
articles.summary: Talks conclude: Microsoft gets the gig

articles.title: CapitaLand acquires stake in Osaka data center from Mitsui
articles.summary: Also buys industrial site in Singapore set to host Keppel's floating data center

articles.title: Jazz and Zong launch 5G services in Pakistan
articles.summary: Pakistan's telcos are wasting no time in launching the service

articles.title: Oracle reveals Hosted Dedicated Region offering
articles.summary: Also adds new UK regions for Oracle Database@AWS

articles.title: Developer Krambu looks to build AI data center in Missoula County, Montana
articles.summary: The data center would be constructed on the old Bonner Mill Industrial Park

articles.title: 5 principles for 800 VDC in AI data centers
articles.summary: Rack-level architectures as the immediate enabler for 800 VDC adoption in AI data centers

articles.title: FuelCell Energy launches 12.5MW modular energy solution for data center sector
articles.summary: Will expand manufacturing facility by more than three times to meet demand

articles.title: TotalEnergies relinquishes leases for two US offshore wind projects, exiting the market
articles.summary: Will invest nearly $1bn into natural gas

articles.title: Puget Sound Energy’s vehicle-to-home pilot combines demand response, peak shaving, resilience
articles.summary: The test will use electric vehicle batteries for demand response and residential peak shaving while also making their storage capacity available during power outages.

articles.title: DOE extends emergency operations at 2 Indiana coal plants
articles.summary: Since December the plants “have proven critical” to operations in the Midcontinent ISO region, DOE said. Sierra Club says they cost consumers almost $200,000 per day.

articles.title: Utilities must ask AI vendors these questions to meet critical infrastructure protection standards
articles.summary: Utilities deploying AI tools may be creating a compliance gap that will become visible only when auditors start asking questions, writes Eric Swidey, founder of Thirty Seven Inc.

articles.title: NextEra to develop 9.5 GW of gas in Texas, Pennsylvania
articles.summary: The projects are part of a $550 billion deal with Japan that also includes 3 GW of nuclear in Tennessee and Alabama, and 9.2 GW of gas generation in Ohio, federal officials say.

articles.title: Maryland ratepayer advocate calls for greater transmission oversight as costs rise
articles.summary: Costs to customers in the state could reach $5.4 billion for transmission built from 2031 through 2035, compared with $7.1 billion spread over the previous 20 years, according to the advocate.

articles.title: Better grid utilization could save customers $170B: Brattle report
articles.summary: However, the report’s lead author said that “we need regulatory models that reward utilities for pursuing this opportunity.”

articles.title: 5-year waits and rising costs: How demand is redefining the gas turbine market
articles.summary: Lengthy lead times are likely to continue for now, and reliability in that environment depends on early, informed decisions, writes Electric Power Research Institute Senior Program Manager Bobby Noble.

articles.title: ‘Emergencies’ requiring coal plants to stay open need not be imminent, DOE tells court
articles.summary: States, environmental groups and others have sued the U.S. Department of Energy over its repeated emergency orders to run the J.H. Campbell plant in West Olive, Michigan, saying it failed to show the emergency need.

articles.title: Securing the last mile: Distribution visibility for a stable grid
articles.summary: As the last mile grows more complex, real-time distribution visibility helps utilities uncover hidden risks, validate assets and support new loads without disruption.

articles.title: DOE taps SoftBank arm to develop 9.2 GW of gas generation in Ohio
articles.summary: SB Energy, a subsidiary of Japan’s SoftBank Group, is also investing $4.2 billion with AEP Ohio to upgrade and build new transmission lines in Southern Ohio.

articles.title: Deep Fission begins drilling first data acquisition well
articles.summary: California-based startup Deep Fission, which aims to place small modular reactors in boreholes a mile underground, has begun drilling the first of three planned data acquisition wells in Parsons, Kansas, where it is building its pilot project.

articles.title: Second tier installed for Leningrad inner containment building
articles.summary: The installation of the second tier at Leningrad Nuclear Power Plant's seventh unit means the inner containment building has now reached a height of 22 metres.

articles.title: Arup to support delivery of the UK's first SMR
articles.summary: Multinational professional services firm Arup has been appointed by Great British Energy - Nuclear to provide early-phase foundation engineering and design support for the construction of its small modular reactor project at Wylfa on the island of Anglesey, North Wales.

articles.title: Construction of Bushehr nuclear power units 'remains a priority'
articles.summary: Rosatom Director General Alexei Likhachev has said that a further 150 people evacuated from Iran have arrived back in Moscow, adding that "the construction itself - the second and third units - remains a top priority for the corporation".

articles.title: First San'ao unit connected to the grid
articles.summary: Unit 1 of the San'ao nuclear power plant has begun supplying electricity to the grid for the first time, China General Nuclear announced. The unit is the first of six Hualong One (HPR1000) reactors planned for the site in Zhejiang province.

articles.title: First new Kursk unit reaches full power
articles.summary: The first VVER-TOI unit at the Kursk II Nuclear Power Plant in Russia has had its power increased to 100% as its commissioning process continues.

articles.title: Planning for Swedish SMR plant proceeds
articles.summary: Swedish lead-cooled small modular reactor technology developer Blykalla said it plans to proceed with the next phase of planning for a power plant in Norrsundet, Gävle, in east central Sweden, after initial assessments confirmed that the site offers suitable conditions.

articles.title: X-energy, Talen to assess deployment of multiple SMR plants
articles.summary: US advanced nuclear technology developer X-energy Reactor Company has signed a Letter of Intent with Talen Energy Corporation to assess deploying X-energy's XE-100 small modular reactors in Pennsylvania and across the PJM Interconnection Regional Transmission Organization market.

articles.title: Aalo completes assembly of experimental reactor
articles.summary: Aalo Atomics has held a ceremony to unveil its completed Critical Test Reactor at the Idaho National Laboratory. The company said it expects the reactor to achieve criticality "well before" the 4 July deadline.

articles.title: Early construction landmarks for Chinese units
articles.summary: The giant CA20 structural module of Bailong nuclear power plant's unit 1 has been lifted into place - and the first steam generator moved into position at Lufeng nuclear power plant's unit 6.

articles.title: Vietnam, Russia sign agreement on new nuclear plant
articles.summary: An intergovernmental agreement has been signed on cooperation in the construction of the Ninh Thuan 1 Nuclear Power Plant in Vietnam, to feature two VVER‑1200 reactors, with the new Leningrad units as the reference project.

articles.title: Application submitted for Swedish SMR plant
articles.summary: Kärnfull Next has submitted an application to build a power plant based on small modular reactors in the municipality of Valdemarsvik in Östergötland county in southeastern Sweden. It is the first application under the country’s new Act on Government Approval of Nuclear Facilities.

articles.title: Uzbekistan and Russia mark SMR construction progress
articles.summary: Russia and Uzbekistan have signed a roadmap for nuclear cooperation, as initial concrete was poured as part of preparations for the construction of the first small modular reactor at Uzbekistan’s first nuclear power plant.

articles.title: Rwanda 'making significant progress' on nuclear energy programme
articles.summary: Rwanda plans to have its first small modular reactor operational in the early-2030s, and an International Atomic Energy Agency mission has outlined steps taken so far.

articles.title: IAEA and Russia discuss Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant situation
articles.summary: International Atomic Energy Agency Director General Rafael Mariano Grossi described the talks with Rosatom Director General Alexei Likhachev in Moscow as "comprehensive and timely".

articles.title: UK implementing nuclear regulatory review recommendations
articles.summary: Three months on from the publication of the final report of the Nuclear Regulatory Taskforce, the UK government has outlined its plans to speed up nuclear delivery. All reforms are expected to be completed by the end of next year, subject to legislative timelines.

articles.title: Regulatory justification for Rolls‑Royce SMR
articles.summary: UK Secretary of State for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs, Emma Reynolds, has decided to provide regulatory justification for the Rolls‑Royce SMR design - the first small modular reactor to receive this approval.

articles.title: APS to seek fresh Palo Verde life extension
articles.summary: Arizona Public Service has officially informed the US Nuclear Regulatory Commission that it wants to renew the operating licences for the Palo Verde Generating Station for a further 20 years.

articles.title: 'Projectile' hit 350 metres from Bushehr nuclear reactor - IAEA
articles.summary: The International Atomic Energy Agency has said that "following information from Iran of a projectile incident on Tuesday evening, the IAEA can confirm that a structure 350 metres from the Bushehr NPP reactor was hit and destroyed".

articles.title: Poland’s radioactive waste management reviewed by IAEA mission
articles.summary: An International Atomic Energy Agency team of experts has praised progress made by Poland in safely managing its radioactive waste, and recommended further steps as the country moves ahead with its nuclear power programme.
